Diffing Against the Previous State

ticket.assigned and ticket.status_changed only fire on a genuine change — which means updateTicket needs to know what the ticket looked like before.

ticket.created only ever happens once per ticket, so there's nothing to compare against. ticket.assigned and ticket.status_changed are different: updateTicket runs on every PATCH, whether or not the field either event cares about actually changed. Emitting ticket.assigned just because a ticket with an agent already assigned got saved again — same agent, some unrelated field edited — would notify that agent for nothing.

Telling "changed" from "already was this" needs the previous row to compare against, so the controller now passes one in:

// Figure 5.3: the existence check it already ran gets reused, not repeated (src/controllers/ticket.controller.js, excerpt)
const ticket = await ticketService.updateTicket(req.params.id, req.body, existing);

existing isn't a new query — it's the same lookup updateTicket's controller already had to run first to confirm the ticket exists at all (Lesson 4's "read before write" pattern), just no longer thrown away once that check passes. The service uses it to diff:

// Figure 5.4: two independent diffs against `previous`, each its own event (src/services/ticket.service.js, excerpt)
export const updateTicket = async (id, changes, previous) => {
  const ticket = await prisma.ticket.update({
    where: { id },
    data: changes,
    include: { customer: userSummary, assignedAgent: userSummary },
  });

  if (ticket.assignedAgentId !== null && ticket.assignedAgentId !== previous.assignedAgentId) {
    domainEvents.emit(EVENTS.TICKET_ASSIGNED, ticket);
  }

  if (ticket.status !== previous.status) {
    domainEvents.emit(EVENTS.TICKET_STATUS_CHANGED, ticket, previous.status);
  }

  return ticket;
};

Each if is answering a different, specific question. The first isn't just "did assignedAgentId change" — !== null also rules out un-assigning a ticket counting as an assignment worth emailing someone about. The second compares status the same way, and passes previous.status as a second argument alongside the updated ticket — the listeners in the next few topics need to say "moved from open to resolved," which means someone has to remember what it moved from, and updateTicket is the last place that's cheaply true.
